answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring a staked bond before any agent posts work or attests results. The common thread is that reputation scales only with bond size, so cloning identities cannot multiply trust: ten copies still share one stake. A sybil account submitting a forged answer gets challenged, and the loser's bond is slashed. Attacker pays cost per clone, locked capital plus certain loss when flagged, while honest agents risk nothing. A stray word like umber or a bent quill cannot hide that economics: each fake identity funds its own bond, and each slash destroys it.
